meta.note: Three of these four scenarios happened. The fourth did not and may never. Where a figure could not be verified from a real source it is held at zero and marked, rather than filled in with something plausible. A blank cell in a stress test is more honest than a confident guess, and you can see exactly which cells are blank.

scenarios.name: The 2008 crash
scenarios.summary: Global shares lost about two fifths of their value in twelve months. Bonds and gold went up. This is the textbook case for owning things that do not all move together.
scenarios.headline: From its October 2007 peak to its March 2009 low, the MSCI World index fell 57.8 percent. That is seventeen months, not twelve, and it is the number people actually lived through.

scenarios.name: The Covid crash
scenarios.summary: A third of the value of global shares gone in twenty-three trading days. The fastest fall of that size on record. Then it was all back within months.
scenarios.headline: Global shares fell 34 percent in about five weeks, and the same index finished the calendar year up 15.9 percent. Anyone who sold in March locked in the loss and missed the recovery.

scenarios.name: The 1970s inflation shock
scenarios.summary: The scenario almost nobody models. Shares and bonds fell together while prices rose 22 percent. Gold nearly tripled. Diversifying across shares and bonds alone did not save anyone.
scenarios.headline: US shares lost 37 percent in cash terms over two years and 49 percent in real terms once inflation is taken out. Bonds gained 5.7 percent in cash terms and lost about 13 percent in real terms. Both of the things a normal portfolio is made of failed at the same time.

scenarios.name: A reordering
scenarios.period: No period. This has not happened.
scenarios.summary: The United States loses its position at the centre of the financial system over a decade. The dollar falls hard, US assets de-rate, and capital moves toward Asia, the Gulf and elsewhere.
scenarios.headline: Every number in this scenario is an assumption, not a forecast. Nobody has data on a thing that has not occurred. Change the numbers and watch what happens: that is the entire point of this panel.
